# Quality-gate boundary review (2026-10-22)

Scope: read-only review of the new `cmd/quality-gate/**`, `docs/quality-boundaries.md`, and `.claude/skills/quality-gate-adopt/SKILL.md`, plus their decision-provider dependency. The command was untracked at review time, so there is no committed baseline for a differential security claim. Fathom `review_diff` and root/file `obligations` were consulted; its review was partial and obligation compilation stale/incomplete. Findings below came from source and executable probes at the time reported.

## Findings

**F1 · P1 · CI defaults to a mutable policy** — `cmd/quality-gate/main.go:49,101-106,190-193` defaults `--policy-ref` to `HEAD` even for `--boundary ci` with `--revision`. A common CI checkout has `HEAD` at the proposed commit, so that commit can weaken its own policy. Disposable repository repro: base policy has `json-valid`; candidate deletes that rule and commits invalid `{broken` in `data.json`. `quality-gate check --boundary ci --base BASE --revision CANDIDATE` exits 0/pass. Adding `--policy-ref BASE` exits 1/hold. The guide's safe example at `docs/quality-boundaries.md:35` does not protect a caller who omits the flag. Require an explicit trusted policy ref at CI/revision enforcement, and test the omission.

**F2 · P1 · Git plumbing can fetch missing objects** — `cmd/quality-gate/git.go:55-68,271-285` filters inherited `GIT_*` variables but does not set `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`. A partial clone may invoke its configured promisor remote when `cat-file` sizes or reads a missing blob, crossing the offline/no-provider boundary without `--allow-remote`. In a disposable `--filter=blob:none` clone with a local `file://` promisor remote, the gate's exact Git argv/environment made `cat-file -s` succeed on an absent blob; the same call with `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` failed. Set it for all Git plumbing and surface missing objects as unknown. No external network was used in this probe.

**F3 · P1 · Missing provider model can pass the resolved-model pin** — `cmd/quality-gate/model.go:202-205,229-238` trusts `decision.Response.Model` for the hold clear. The OpenAI adapter at `foundations/decision/openai/openai.go:193-199` substitutes the requested model if the provider response omits `model`. An `httptest` response containing a valid `clear` answer but no model returned `Model="pinned"`, `Choice="clear"`. With matching calibration, the gate has no evidence of the resolved model yet can clear the hold. Make missing provider model identity distinguishable from the request and require an attested response model for holds.

**F4 · P2 · CUE and Go policy contracts disagree** — `cmd/quality-gate/schema.cue:50-52` constrains calibration `site` to `#ID`, which rejects the slash-delimited `policy/boundary/site` binding required by `cmd/quality-gate/model.go:297-299`; the schema's `provider` enum also omits runtime's `typesafe-openrouter` identity. A runtime-shaped calibration caused `cue vet -c cmd/quality-gate/schema.cue policy.json -d '#Policy'` to fail on `calibration.site`. Conversely, adding `max_bytes` to a `conflict-markers` rule passed that CUE vet but fails `validatePolicy` at `cmd/quality-gate/policy.go:123-126`. Align schema and runtime, then test both against the same positive and negative fixtures. `cue vet` without `-d '#Policy'` returned success for this invalid calibration, so adoption instructions should show the explicit definition check.

## Covered behavior and limits

- `go test -race ./cmd/quality-gate` passed. Source and tests cover staged/index objects, linked worktrees, malformed policy JSON, multi-ref push, new refs, deletions, missing bases, model drift, calibration, cache, and hard-failure precedence.
- Remote provider calls were not made. Hook installation, live Lefthook merging, protected CI status, and real provider attestation were not verified; the guide correctly treats those as separate adoption proofs.
- Reports omit raw source and credential values. Shadow cache is advisory in the reviewed code. The four findings above are concrete boundary failures or contract drift; no broader codebase claim is made.

## Disposition after fixes

- **F1 resolved in current source.** `main.go:68-95` rejects CI and pre-publish revision enforcement without an explicit policy ref. The disposable CLI run returned 2 for omitted `--policy-ref`; the trusted-base fixture returns 1 under its original rule. `TestCLICIRequiresExplicitTrustedPolicy` passed under the focused race suite. The CLI cannot prove that a caller-supplied ref is independently trusted; CI wiring remains an adoption check.
- **F2 resolved in current source.** `git.go:64-68` sets `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`. `TestPromisedBlobNeverFetched` verifies a promised missing blob stays missing and revision capture fails closed. It passed under the focused race suite.
- **F3 resolved in current source.** `model.go:354-459` checks exactly one explicit wire `model` against the expected resolved model before adapter decoding. The `httptest` regression covers missing, duplicate, wrong, malformed, oversized, and matching responses; all passed under the focused race suite. The added clear-calibration test prevents unrelated concern accuracy from certifying false clears.
- **F4 resolved for the reported mismatches.** `schema.cue:40-117` now accepts the slash-delimited site and provider identity and rejects irrelevant rule options. Direct `cue vet -c ... -d '#Policy'` accepted the calibrated fixture and rejected stray `max_bytes`; the cross-kind parity test passed. This is targeted parity evidence, not an exhaustive equivalence proof.
- `go test -race ./cmd/quality-gate` passed again after fixes, including report-output failure and unsupported-flag tests. Independent adoption evidence is in `skill-forward-test.md`.

## Final delta review

- CI and pre-publish enforcement now require a committed `--revision` and explicit `--policy-ref`; staged input is rejected even with an explicit ref. Text and JSON report write errors return exit 2, and unused command flags fail before repository I/O. The race suite covers these cases.
- Empty Git blobs retain a non-nil empty byte slice, so content rules evaluate them; shadow-cache reads are bounded to 1 MiB; `require-companion` also checks deleted trigger paths and requires a surviving changed companion. Targeted tests passed.
- After the final policy/schema edits, `go test -race ./cmd/quality-gate`, CUE vet of the default policy against `#Policy`, `gofmt -l`, and `git diff --check` passed. No new concrete boundary bypass was found in this delta.
- CUE and runtime validation have targeted parity tests, but exhaustive equivalence is unproven; CUE vet can accept an omitted required field in some forms, so the runtime decoder checks collection presence. Fathom's reported 5/8 review dimensions and stale obligations are not a clean static proof. Hook/CI adoption and real provider behavior remain outside this source review.
